lines.x: You know this isn't exactly the work I'm best suited for... right?

Didn't think Rhodes Island would go through something that big while I was gone. You holding up all right?—Oh? So you do remember I've always wanted your job. Then you'd better work hard, because I sure haven't forgotten that goal.

Back then Medical figured we weren't ready. Well, look now—I brought everyone home without a scratch, and we got the Ursus office up and running. You're saying I wasn't too optimistic about it myself at the time? We pulled it off. Can't I enjoy it a little longer?

Istina put together a new reading list for me. She's right—if you want to bring more people together, you have to learn a different kind of knowledge. You're headed to the library anyway? Then tell the librarian for me: I'm taking my time with those dozen-odd books I borrowed, and I'll return them... within the deadline, more or less.
Oh, this? My new weapon. Took it off some bastard. People who lean on power that isn't theirs to push others around—I don't mind knocking every last one of them down.

There was a while when I seriously considered disbanding the Ursus Student Self-Governing Group. But later I figured—it isn't bad for everyone to have somewhere they can lean on without worrying... Yeah. Rhodes Island is that kind of place for us too.

Don't worry too much. We ran into some trouble, but everyone pulled through, and Zoya's officially joined the Self-Governing Group. Gummy's been a little out of it lately, though—because of her parents. We're all trying to figure out how to help her... If you think of anything good, be sure to tell us.

When did I start wanting to go back to Ursus? That place buried my parents, and it nearly buried the rest of us too. I used to hate it... I ran from it. But sooner or later there comes a moment with nowhere left to back down to, and that's when you learn you have to stand up and face it.

You're just like Istina. Before doing something 'stupid,' you always dig up some grand principle first. I can't be bothered to listen, but I know that when it comes to what should be done, we've always been on the same page. Fine, have your principles. Either way, every wall and bulwark they've built is getting smashed open by us.
I'm heading out for a walk. If you feel like moving too, come find me outside.
Reporting in first: the mission to establish an office in Ursus is complete... I have to write up an operation report too? What a pain...
So when's the real fight?
The medals get handed out all over again? Because that's what the procedure says? If Ursus's nobles were even half as thorough as you people, I'd never have made it out of that blockade zone.

Come to think of it, who makes Rhodes Island's medals? I want a few made with the Self-Governing Group's crest on them. The first batch goes to Istina and the others, obviously, and after that... well, it never hurts to keep a few in reserve.
Fighting's still the easiest thing.
Same as always?
Make it quick.
Hah. Here's hoping they're tougher than they look.
Put me where the crowd is.
What's your call?
I'm here. Everyone hold.
Here I go!
Anyone tired of living, step up!
Who's next?
All for one, and one for all!
Charge with me!
Heh... Now that hit the spot!
That was barely a warm-up.
Fast on their feet, at least...
Tch. Leave the rest to me. Don't embarrass yourself like that again.
Phew, back again...
You've got that much free time...? Forget it, do what you want.
Good timing. Let's go see how everyone's doing.
Arknights.
Ugh, every year Rhodes Island gets this rowdy on this day... Oh, you're here. Try this—pancakes I made with Gummy. We're heading straight out to have some fun after. Coming?
Hey. You doing all right lately?
Here. An Ursus leather coat I brought back—figured it'd suit you. What, the Self-Governing Group's mark on it? I drew that myself. Got a problem with it? ...Good... Happy birthday, Doctor.

There was a time the Self-Governing Group existed only so we could 'stay alive.' Now that we're all here on Rhodes Island, I can't help thinking further ahead... At the very least, here's where I stand: when everyone runs off down their own road, I won't let a single one of them fall.
